pack_layout:
ONE zip format, extension .stvdpack (proposed; no conflict check done). It is used for four kinds of pack:
- single-component packs
- category bundles
- per-category thumbnail preview packs
- user exports
Entries follow Phase 5.2: deflate JSON/GLB/TXT, store PNG/JPG.

Inside a pack:
  pack.json                                              PackManifest; lists every file with SHA-256 and size
  components/<namespace>/<slug>/<semver>/component.json  ComponentManifest (at most 256 KiB)
  components/<namespace>/<slug>/<semver>/thumbnail.png   at most 512x512, at most 2 MiB
  geometry/<sha256>.glb                                  normalized GLB, shared by every component in the pack
  textures/<sha256>.png or .jpg
  licenses/<sha256>.txt                                  full license texts (KiCad LICENSE.md, MIT/Apache texts)
  catalog/index.json + catalog/index.json.minisig        bundles only, optional: offline verification as official
No other paths are accepted.

Granularity, weighed:
(A) One pack per category.
  - Pros: few requests, simple hosting.
  - Cons: all-or-nothing downloads when you need three parts; one LED fix re-ships and re-versions the whole category; versioning, revocation and updates are coupled; bigger cost to verify and extract per install.
(B) One pack per component.
  - Pros: smallest downloads; independent semver, updates and revocation per component; immutable content-addressed URLs; parallel downloads; dedup on disk through the global content store.
  - Cons: many HTTP requests for bulk installs; GitHub caps a release at 1000 assets; shared geometry is downloaded twice (but stored once).
DECISION (proposed): (B) is the canonical unit, plus two derived artifacts regenerated at each catalog publish:
- category bundles (the same format holding N components), for 'Download all Electrical' and for air-gapped installs via 'Install from file', with the signed index embedded;
- per-category preview packs (thumbnails only), so browsing a category costs one request.
Every install is recorded per component@version, so bundle and single installs coexist and dedupe.

Size evidence (KiCad STEP sources, GitLab API, high confidence, but only 3 samples):
- LED_THT.3dshapes/LED_D5.0mm.step = 23,819 B
- Resistor_THT.3dshapes/R_Axial_DIN0207_L6.3mm_D2.5mm_P10.16mm_Horizontal.step = 24,557 B
- Button_Switch_THT.3dshapes/SW_PUSH_6mm.step = 179,934 B
Expected per-component pack size: tens to hundreds of KB. This is an estimate with LOW confidence; tessellated GLB size is unknown until the pipeline is built.

Local install layout. It lives under Tauri appLocalDataDir, not the cache dir, because OS cleaners may purge caches and content must work offline. appLocalDataDir resolves to:
- Windows: {FOLDERID_LocalAppData}/com.studiovd.desktop
- Linux: $XDG_DATA_HOME, or ~/.local/share, then /com.studiovd.desktop
(source: tauri 2.12.2 src/path/desktop.rs, high confidence)
  library/catalogs/<catalogId>/index.json, index.json.minisig, state.json
  library/store/geometry|textures|licenses/<sha256>.*    global content-addressed store
  library/components/<namespace>/<slug>/<semver>/component.json, thumbnail.png, origin.json
  library/previews/<catalogId>/<category>/<sha256>.png
  library/staging/<uuid>/                                 in-progress installs; wiped at startup
  library/installed.json                                  registry; rebuilt from components/ if missing or corrupt
Only Rust commands write here. JS gets read-only asset-protocol scope on components/, store/ and previews/, for thumbnails and ghost previews.

Content pipeline (separate repo, CI):
- Sources: component.src JSON plus upstream STEP pinned to a commit (e.g. gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-packages3D).
- Tessellation: occt-import-js (same as Phase 4.4).
- Normalization and analysis: the app's own src/core code (Phase 4.5/4.6), so library GLBs follow the same invariants.
- GLB writing: @gltf-transform/core 4.5.1 (MIT). Whether three's GLTFExporter runs in Node is UNKNOWN, so it is not relied on.
- Validation: Khronos gltf-validator (npm 2.0.0-dev.3.10, Apache-2.0).
- Thumbnails: rendered by headless Chromium with the app renderer.
- Output: packs, bundles, previews, index.json; then minisign signing; then upload to a draft release that is published as immutable.
mapping_to_scene_json: ComponentDefKey is a natural key, '<id>@<version>#<first 12 hex of manifestSha256>', not a UUID. It is shared by every instance of one definition, so the snapshot is stored once. The hash suffix stops a sideloaded fake 'official/x@1.0.0' from merging with the real one. Every other new ID is crypto.randomUUID() (CLAUDE.md §3).

COPY rule: at insert time a Rust command library_materialize(defKey, workspace) copies every geometry/<sha>.glb, texture and license text the definition references from library/store into the project workspace (Phase 4.1), skipping any SHA that is already present. Bytes never cross IPC as JSON. After this, the .stvd holds everything it needs and opens on a machine that never downloaded the library. Generator-backed parts copy the GLB that was produced; it is never regenerated on open.

Per-entity mapping, with manifest M and instance pose T (component frame -> world, rigid):
- assets[sha] ??= GeometryAsset, with bbox, triCount, faces, volume, centroid and watertight recomputed by the Phase 4.6 analysis. Pack-declared numbers are only checked, never trusted.
- textures[sha] ??= {...}.
- materials: a builtin key reuses an unmodified project material with the same builtinKey, else creates one from the Phase 6 preset. An inline material creates one MaterialId per (def, key), shared across instances until the user edits it.

parts: one PartId per M.parts[k]:
- position/quaternion = T * M.parts[k].transform (rigid only, never scaled)
- assetId = sha; materialId (+ materialSlots)
- collider = M.parts[k].collider; massOverrideKg = mass.kg (+ comOverrideMm)
- grounded = placement.groundIfFirst and the scene had no parts, else false
- parentId = the instance's scene-graph group (groupId)
- name = part.name, shown under the group named by the designator ('M2')
- componentRef = { instance, key }

anchors: one AnchorId per M.anchors[k], with partId mapped. kind and the part-local frame are copied VERBATIM: part-local frames are unaffected by T. source = { kind: 'component', instance, key }. name and interface metadata are kept for snap suggestions.

mates: one MateId per M.mates[k], with anchorA/anchorB mapped. type, flip, angleOffset (rad), limits, contactsEnabled copied; suppressed = false. The authored design pose already satisfies these mates, so the Phase 8 snap is a no-op check (assert < 1e-9 mm). Fixed internal mates are merged into one rigid body by the Phase 8.4 union-find, as for any fixed mate. If the drop snapped to a suggested mate, ONE extra user-owned Mate is created between the component anchor and the target anchor. It is not part of the instance, so deleting the instance asks whether to remove it too.

schematic: blockDefs[newId] is created once per ComponentDef from M.schematic.block, and its id is stored in componentDefs[key].blockDefId. One node is pushed: { id, type: 'component', blockDefId, position, data: { label: designator, paramValues: {}, componentInstanceId } }. An empty paramValues means 'use the definition defaults', which makes later updates diff-able. Simulation results stay in the session store keyed by node/port id (CLAUDE.md §4), never in node data. An unknown SimModelId (a project made with a newer app) becomes a solver diagnostic 'needs newer StudioVD' and never blocks opening the file.

bindings: one BindingId per M.bindings[k]. Local refs resolve to MateId, PartId, AnchorId and nodeId+port/param key. ExternalSlot refs produce { status: 'unresolved', prompt }, inactive until the user picks the target in the Phase 12 binding editor.

components[instanceId] records every created entity by LocalKey. That makes these operations deterministic:
- delete instance: deletes its parts, anchors, internal mates, node and bindings
- duplicate: re-inserted from the snapshot, works offline
- unlink: drops componentRef, keeps provenance for credits
- update: matches by key

Phase 10.6 part<->node association for NON-library parts uses the same ComponentInstance record with origin { kind: 'project' } and no def, or a def created on the fly. This makes Save-as-component a straight serialization of an existing instance.
Credits are DERIVED, never stored: selector(componentDefs used by live or unlinked instances) -> grouped license list. Save GC drops componentDefs, assets and license texts that nothing references.

Updates (only after the user explicitly refreshes the catalog): when the catalog has a higher version of a componentDef with the same MAJOR, the instance shows a badge. Applying an update is ONE undo entry:
- swap assetIds by part key
- replace anchor frames by key; external mates stay attached and are re-snapped through Phase 8, with a preview of any part that would move
- keep node paramValues the user changed, take new defaults for the rest
- keep user material and mass edits
- removed keys suppress dependent external mates and list them
A MAJOR change is offered as Replace, not Update. Revoked 'security' entries put a warning badge on instances; project data is never deleted automatically.
insertion_flow: 1. Library tab (left sidebar, PLAN 2.14) has five sources: Installed, My components, Generators (in-app; always offline), Online catalog, Schematic primitives (Phase 10.3). Search runs in a worker over name, tags, MPN and family. The list is virtualized. Each card shows the thumbnail, name, key params, a domain icon, the license short-SPDX, and badges: Official / User / Unverified / Needs newer app / Update available.

2. Online is opt-in and explicit (offline-first: no implicit requests). 'Browse online catalog' or 'Refresh' fetches index.json + .minisig (verified in Rust), then the preview pack of each category the user opens. Clicking Download on an uninstalled card, or 'Download category', runs an install job with progress, cancel and errors. Before download, a 'License & source' popover shows the geometry and data licenses.

3. Drag starts on pointerdown on an installed card. It uses pointer events with setPointerCapture plus a DOM ghost, NOT HTML5 DnD. Reason: Tauri docs say disabling dragDropEnabled 'is required to use HTML5 drag and drop on the frontend on Windows' (tauri-utils 2.10.1 config.rs, high confidence), and Phase 4 wants the native OS file-drop events for importing CAD files.

4. Over the 3D viewport the DOM ghost is swapped for a 3D ghost. Ghost geometry comes from library/store through the asset protocol, or from a worker for generator presets. The ghost is TRANSIENT state (a ref, never Zustand). Placement is resolved each frame through the BVH raycast (Phase 4.6), in priority order:
(a) a compatible anchor on a scene part within the snap radius: the AnchorInterface type and gender complement each other and diameter is within tolerance. The preview uses the PLAN section 2 formula M_B = M_A F_A R_flip R_z(phi) F_B^-1 and shows the suggested mate label.
(b) the surface under the cursor: placementAnchor z aligned to -normal, origin at the hit point.
(c) the ground grid y = 0.
Keys during the drag: R rotates 90 degrees about the placement axis; Alt skips snapping; Esc cancels.

5. Dropping on the viewport:
- check requires.app and sim-model/generator majors; if unmet, the drop is blocked with an explanation
- library_materialize copies blobs into the workspace (Rust, skips existing SHAs)
- ONE store action insertComponent({ defKey, pose, snap? }) inside a single zundo entry creates every entity listed in mapping_to_scene_json, plus the snap mate if (a) applied
- the node is placed at the next free grid slot near the centre of the visible schematic viewport
- the designator is the next free number for the prefix (LED3)
- the new instance is selected and cross-selection highlights the node (Phase 10.6)
- a toast offers Undo
6. Dropping on the schematic pane does the same, but the node goes at the drop position and the parts go at a free spot in 3D: beside the scene bbox on +X, ungrounded, no snap.

7. Keyboard and accessibility path: Enter on a focused card inserts at the origin. If an anchor is selected and compatible, it inserts snapped to that anchor. A context menu offers 'Insert', 'Insert at selected anchor', 'Show license'.

8. After insert: clicking the instance in 3D selects the whole component (group) first; double-click enters it to select single parts. The Properties panel has Component (designator, version, params proxy to the node), 'Source & license', 'Unlink from library' and 'Update'. Undo removes every entity at once. Copied blobs stay in the workspace until GC at save; they are content-addressed, so this is harmless.

9. Gestures: the drag preview never touches the store. Only the drop commits. This follows CLAUDE.md §4: transient per-frame state lives outside Zustand, and a continuous gesture makes one undo entry.
procedural_components:
Rule: CODE ships only in the app; downloaded packs are pure data.

Generator modules:
- Generators are versioned pure-TS modules at src/core/generators/<id>/v<major>.ts: { id, major, version, paramsSchema (zod), presets?, generate(params) -> { bodies: Record<LocalKey, MeshData>, manifestPartial } }.
- manifestPartial holds anchors (e.g. the bore and OD axes of a bearing, the head-bearing face and shank axis of a screw), parts, internal mates and the default material.
- They run in a Web Worker (src/workers/generate.worker.ts) and go through the same Phase 4.5 normalization and SHA-256 path as imports.

How the two kinds coexist:
- A data component can reference a generator: GeometryRef { kind: 'generated', generator, generatorMajor, params, output }.
- The catalog lists GeneratorPresetEntry items (e.g. 'gen/bearing-608-2rsh', with SKF 608-2RSH d=8, D=22, B=7 mm and mass 0.0119 kg; source https://www.skf.com/group/products/rolling-bearings/ball-bearings/deep-groove-ball-bearings/productid-608-2RSH; confidence medium, taken from a search-result summary). Their tiny packs carry only component.json (names, mass, datasheet refs) and a thumbnail. The geometry comes from the app.
- The Generators source in the Library tab works fully offline with free parameters. Data packs can therefore add new presets without new code; new shapes need an app release.
- An unknown or newer generator major shows the card as 'Needs newer StudioVD'. A project that already contains generated parts still opens, because the GLB was copied in.

Determinism:
- ECMAScript defines Math.sin and Math.exp as 'implementation-approximated' (tc39 ecma262 spec.html, high confidence). Generator output may therefore differ in the last bits between WebView2 (V8, Windows) and WebKitGTK (JavaScriptCore, Linux).
- So: the generated GLB is persisted in the project and never regenerated implicitly. Hashes are not expected to match across machines. Golden tests compare geometry within a tolerance and assert that anchor keys are stable, not that bytes are equal.

Editing and freezing:
- 'Edit parameters' on a generated instance regenerates a new asset, keeps anchor, part and mate keys (so external mates and bindings survive and are re-snapped), and makes one undo entry.
- 'Save as component' freezes a generated part into a plain data component.

Data tables:
- Standard dimension tables (ISO/DIN fasteners, bearing series) ship IN the app next to the generator code, so they are reviewed and tested with it.
- Legal status of copying values from ISO/DIN standards (copyright / EU database rights): UNKNOWN; see open questions.
- Permissive sources: cq_warehouse is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file, high confidence). BOLTS is GPL-3.0 and FreeCAD_FastenersWB is GPL-2.0 (repository LICENSE files, high confidence), so they are not suitable to copy into the app without a licensing decision.

Proposed v1 generators: bearing.deepGroove (outer + inner ring + revolute), fastener.iso4762 (socket head cap screw), nut.hex, washer.plain, shaft/rod/tube, plate/box/cylinder primitives, gear.spur (module, teeth). These cover mechanical parts with no downloads.

How 'never executable' is enforced:
- The schema has no field that accepts code. Behaviour is only an in-app SimModelId, GeneratorId or BuiltinSymbolId reference, or a sandbox expression.
- A file-type allowlist (JSON, GLB, PNG, JPG, TXT) is enforced.
- GLB external URIs and required extensions are rejected.
- Symbols are app-drawn; packs never contain SVG.
- There is no plugin or JS loading path at all.
user_components:
'Save as component' writes the SAME format into the user library, so one validator and one insertion path serve everything.

Flow:
1. Select parts or an existing instance, then context menu 'Save as component...'.
2. Dialog fields: name; slug (auto); version (1.0.0, or bumped when overwriting an existing user component: PATCH/MINOR/MAJOR suggested from a key diff); category; tags; designator prefix; description; vendor/MPN optional.
3. Root part and component origin: default = the grounded or first-selected part's frame, or an anchor the user chooses as 'placement'.
4. Anchors: every anchor on the selected parts, each with a checkbox, and the option to mark interface tags.
5. Mates: internal mates (both anchors inside the selection) are included. External mates are listed as 'not saved'.
6. Schematic: if exactly one linked node (Phase 10.6 association or an instance), its blockDef plus current param values become the defaults. Several nodes: v1 asks you to pick one or save without schematic (composite blocks are reserved for schemaVersion 2).
7. Bindings: fully internal bindings are kept. A binding that points outside the selection becomes an ExternalSlot with an auto prompt.
8. Thumbnail: offscreen 256x256 transparent render of the selection from the current or iso view. It travels as raw binary IPC (CLAUDE.md §6).
9. License step:
   - geometry license from presets: 'All rights reserved (mine)' = LicenseRef-StudioVD-UserPrivate, redistributable false; CC0-1.0; CC-BY-4.0; or 'third-party: source URL + SPDX'
   - attribution creators
   - INHERITED licenses of any library parts in the selection are added automatically, as ComponentLicense.inherited and as an AND in the geometry SPDX expression. The user cannot remove them.
10. Writing:
   - a pure core function buildComponentManifest(selection, doc) -> { manifest, blobShas }
   - then the Rust command library_save_user_component(manifestJson, blobShas, thumbnailBytes) copies blobs from the project workspace into library/store, writes components/<ns>/<slug>/<ver>/ atomically (staging + rename), then runs the full pack validator on the result
   - a saved component must pass exactly the checks a downloaded one does
11. Optionally the selection is replaced in place by a linked instance of the new definition.

Namespace:
- per installation, 'u-' + 6 random base32 chars, editable to a publisher name in Settings
- reserved and refused for user or sideloaded content: 'official', 'gen', 'builtin', 'studiovd'

Sharing:
- 'Export pack...' writes an unsigned .stvdpack (single or multi); 'Install from file...' sideloads it with an 'Unverified' badge after confirmation.
- 'Add to my library' on a componentDef inside an opened .stvd harvests it (origin project). If its manifestSha256 matches the cached signed index, it is promoted to Official.
- Non-redistributable components warn on export.

Location: appLocalDataDir/library/components/<user-ns>/... by default; a configurable location is an open question. The registry can be rebuilt from disk.
licensing_and_attribution:
Per-component model:
- ComponentLicense has separate grants for geometry (GLB/textures), data (anchors/params/bindings/text) and thumbnail, plus inherited[] for derived user components.
- Each grant carries: SPDX expression, creators, copyright notice, source URL + revision, a modifications statement, license URL or full text, attributionRequired, redistributable.
- These fields map directly to CC BY-SA 4.0 section 3(a)(1). If shared, you must retain: creator identification, copyright notice, a notice referring to the license, a notice referring to the warranty disclaimer, and a URI to the material; indicate modifications; and include the license text or its URI. 3(a)(2) allows doing this through a URI or hyperlink. 3(b) ShareAlike: adaptations must use the same or a compatible license and may not add Effective Technological Measures. Source: creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/legalcode via the cc-legal-tools-data repo, high confidence.
- MIT requires the notice 'included in all copies or substantial portions', and Apache-2.0 section 4(a) requires giving recipients a copy of the License (SPDX license-list-data texts, high confidence). So for MIT/BSD/Apache content the full text must travel as licenses/<sha>.txt: in packs, in the library store and inside the .stvd.

KiCad content:
- KiCad 3D models are licensed 'CC-BY-SA 4.0' with an exception for electronic designs. KiCad's LICENSE.md also says redistributed library collections 'must be shared under the same license agreement' and 'must also retain attribution information, including the license documents' (https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-packages3D/-/raw/master/LICENSE.md, high confidence).
- SPDX lists 'KiCad-libraries-exception' (license-list-data 3.29.0, 2026-09-16, high confidence). The SPDX expression is therefore 'CC-BY-SA-4.0 WITH KiCad-libraries-exception'; SPDX expressions support WITH and LicenseRef- (spdx-spec v3.0.1 annex, high confidence).
- Our online catalog IS a redistributed collection. Catalog packs of KiCad-derived geometry must stay CC-BY-SA-4.0, credit 'KiCad Libraries contributors', link the source at a pinned commit, state the modifications (tessellated, split, recentred, Y-up) and ship KiCad's LICENSE.md as a license text.

Where licenses are surfaced:
1. Library card: short SPDX badge, and a 'License & source' popover before download and before insert.
2. Instance Properties: a 'Source & license' section.
3. Project Credits dialog (Help > Project credits, also in File > Project info):
   - derived from componentDefs used by live or unlinked instances
   - grouped by license, listing creators, sources, modifications and license links
   - 'Copy' and 'Export CREDITS.txt' buttons
   - a warning when the project holds redistributable:false content
4. .stvd: componentDefs snapshots plus licenses/<sha>.txt carry attribution inside every saved project. A recipient who never downloaded the library still has full notices.
5. Exports:
   - GLB: glTF asset.copyright is 'a copyright message suitable for display to credit the content creator' (Khronos glTF 2.0 asset.schema.json, high confidence). It is set to a short summary, with full structured credits in asset.extras.studiovdCredits.
   - STL has no metadata, so a <name>.credits.txt sidecar is written. Turning that off shows a warning when attributionRequired.
   - Schematic SVG/PNG exports contain only app-drawn symbols, so no third-party credits are needed.
   - 3D screenshots/renders get an optional credits footer (legal status in open questions).
6. App-level credits for in-app generator data and bundled code go in About > Third-party notices, not per project.

Proposed official-catalog license allowlist (enforced in pack CI, PENDING LEGAL REVIEW): CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0 (with or without KiCad-libraries-exception), MIT, BSD-2/3-Clause, Apache-2.0.
Rejected:
- NC licenses: commercial users of StudioVD projects would be excluded.
- ND licenses: tessellation and splitting are adaptations.
- GPL/LGPL for content: copyleft scope over a project file is unclear.
- Vendor or 'free download' models with no-redistribution terms (common on vendor CAD portals). These may live only in a user's private library, marked redistributable:false.
security_rules: Trust root: minisign/Ed25519 public keys are compiled into the Rust binary. Use at least 2 keys for catalogId 'official' (active + offline backup) and rotate them through app updates. Test keys exist only under cfg(test)/debug feature flags and are refused in release builds (a CI assertion checks this). Tauri itself treats updater signatures as mandatory ('This cannot be disabled', tauri-docs updater.mdx, high confidence) and uses minisign-verify 0.3 (tauri-plugin-updater 2.13.2 Cargo.toml, high confidence). Use a separate key for the library, never the updater key.

Index verification (Rust, before JSON parse):
- stream with a 16 MiB cap
- minisign-verify 0.3.0 verify(.., allow_legacy=false): prehashed only; the trusted comment is covered by the global signature
- trusted comment must equal 'studiovd-catalog <id> seq=<n> expires=<t>' and match the JSON fields
- reject sequence < highestSequence (rollback), and the same sequence with different bytes
- refuse installs when expiresAt < now (freeze); installed content keeps working
- reject minAppVersion > app with an 'update StudioVD' message
(Threat names from TUF spec 1.0.37, high confidence.)

Downloads (Rust, reqwest + rustls; never through the webview):
- HTTPS only; at most 5 redirects, each HTTPS
- connect/read timeouts
- abort when received bytes exceed PackEntry.bytes (endless data)
- write to library/staging/<uuid>/
- the SHA-256 must equal the PackId BEFORE the zip is opened
- the request carries no user identifiers: User-Agent 'StudioVD/<ver>'
- proxy: reqwest uses system proxies by default (HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY env vars; Windows/macOS system settings via the default system-proxy feature), reqwest 0.13.5 lib.rs, high confidence
- the webview CSP (Phase 13) never needs external origins, because all library networking runs in Rust

Zip extraction: own loop, NEVER ZipArchive::extract. RUSTSEC-2025-0168 / CVE-2025-29787 (GHSA-94vh-gphv-8pm8) was a symlink-based arbitrary file write in that function for zip 1.3.0 up to (not including) 2.3.0 (rustsec.org via search summary, medium confidence). Use zip >= 8.x, whose ZipFile exposes enclosed_name(), is_symlink(), size() and compressed_size() (zip 8.6.0 source, high confidence).
For each entry:
- require enclosed_name()
- also reject absolute paths, '..', backslash, drive letters, NUL/control chars, paths over 200 bytes, case-insensitive duplicates, Windows reserved names (CON, NUL, COM1...), and trailing dots or spaces
- reject symlinks, encrypted entries, and any path outside the allowlisted patterns
- treat declared sizes as untrusted: count real bytes with Read::take
- per-entry caps (proposed): GLB 64 MiB, PNG/JPG 2 MiB (thumbnail) / 16 MiB (texture), JSON 256 KiB, TXT 256 KiB
- entries: at most 64 per single pack, at most 4096 per bundle
- total uncompressed must not exceed PackEntry.uncompressedBytes or 2 GiB
- compression ratio at most 200:1 per entry
- every entry is listed in pack.json with matching SHA-256 and size; content-addressed names must equal the computed hash
- unlisted entries reject the whole pack
The same module serves .stvd bundles (Phase 5.2).

One validation pipeline is used for every source: online packs, sideloaded .stvdpack, user-library saves, and componentDefs inside an opened .stvd (a project file is untrusted input too). Sideloaded content is 'Unverified' after explicit confirmation. Reserved namespaces (official, gen, builtin, studiovd) are accepted only with a valid official signature or index hash match.

Schema validation (zod, src/core/schema/library):
- .strict() everywhere; every number finite
- vectors unit-length within 1e-6; x orthogonal to z; quaternions normalized; limits min <= max; density > 0; units exist in units.ts
- string length caps; collection caps: parts <= 64, anchors <= 256, mates <= 64, ports <= 64, params <= 128, bindings <= 64, thumbnails <= 4
- referential integrity: every LocalKey reference resolves; mate anchors are internal; binding direction pairs are type-checked
- LocalKey regex; '__proto__', 'constructor' and 'prototype' refused; parsed records stored as Map or null-prototype objects
- unknown SimModelId/GeneratorId majors mark the component 'Needs newer StudioVD' and never crash or block opening
The zod schemas are canonical; Rust checks only container-level invariants and hashes. JSON Schema for the separate content-pipeline repo is generated with zod 4 z.toJSONSchema() (verified present in zod 4.6.5).

GLB checks before use (Rust, cheap):
- magic 'glTF', version 2, chunk lengths consistent with the file size, JSON chunk <= 2 MiB, BIN chunk present
- NO 'uri' on any buffer or image: glTF allows external or data: URIs (Khronos buffer/image schema), and three 0.186.1 GLTFLoader.loadBuffer fetches bufferDef.uri via FileLoader (high confidence), which would be a runtime network or file request
- extensionsRequired must be empty in v1: no Draco or meshopt, which keeps decoder attack surface and hashing simple
- the app recounts triangles and bbox and compares them with the manifest; a mismatch rejects the pack
- recentring check: bbox centre is approximately at the origin
- per-asset triangle cap (proposed 500k) and per-component cap
- pack CI runs Khronos gltf-validator (Apache-2.0)

Images: read the PNG/JPEG header for dimensions BEFORE decoding (thumbnails <= 512x512, textures <= 4096x4096). Decode only through the webview (img / createImageBitmap) from asset-protocol URLs. No SVG, no HTML, no Markdown rendering. All text is plain text through React escaping; dangerouslySetInnerHTML is banned for library data.

Expression sandbox (Phase 10 grammar, applied to pack and user expressions):
- allowed: numbers; identifiers that resolve to declared ports, params and locals; + - * / ^ and unary minus; comparisons; && || !; ?:
- functions, allowlisted and pure: min, max, abs, sqrt, exp, log, pow, clamp, sin, cos, tanh, sign
- not allowed: member access, strings, assignment, loops, recursion, undeclared calls
- limits: <= 2 KiB per expression, <= 512 AST nodes, depth <= 32, <= 64 equations per block; locals must be acyclic
- evaluation: an AST interpreter (also usable with dual numbers for Newton-Raphson Jacobians); never eval or new Function (CLAUDE.md §3); NaN and Inf results become diagnostics
- do not adopt expr-eval: npm latest is 2.0.2 from 2019-09-28 (registry, high confidence), with CVE-2025-12735 (code execution via evaluate variables) and CVE-2025-13204 (prototype pollution) (GitLab advisories / CERT VU#263614, medium confidence)

Filesystem and capabilities:
- library writes happen only in Rust commands (library_install, library_commit_install, library_save_user_component, library_remove, library_gc)
- JS gets read-only asset-protocol scope for library/components, library/store and library/previews, and no fs-plugin write scope
- staging sits on the same volume; install is an atomic rename
- GC never deletes a blob referenced by any installed manifest or open workspace
- every Tauri call goes through src/lib/tauri (CLAUDE.md §3)

URLs inside packs (datasheet, source, license) must be https. They are displayed with their host and opened only via the src/lib/tauri opener wrapper after an explicit confirmation. Packs never trigger navigation or fetches on their own.

Offline-first and privacy: no network request without an explicit user action (Browse/Refresh/Download/Check for updates). A global 'Online library' switch exists (default: ask on first use). Update checks never run automatically on startup.
Revocation: revoked entries with severity 'security' mark installed copies and project instances with a warning. Nothing is deleted silently.

Publishing hygiene:
- sign offline or in a protected CI environment with required reviewers
- publish each catalog as an IMMUTABLE GitHub release (GA 2025-10-28 per GitHub changelog/docs, medium confidence): assets and tag are locked after publish
- pin upstream content to commits
phase_placement:
PLAN.md already has item 1.8, 'Component library design (new requirement, §6 + Phase 14)'. This design fills §6, and approval comes at 1.9.

RECOMMENDATION: keep the name Phase 14 but run it AFTER Phase 12 and BEFORE Phase 13. That way Phase 13's capability audit, perf pass, CSP and installers cover the library's network and install code. The alternative is to renumber it to 13.

Hooks in earlier phases, so that no migration or rework is needed later:
- 2.8: branded IDs ComponentInstanceId/ComponentDefKey and type skeletons. 2.14: Library tab placeholder with sources Installed / My components / Generators / Online / Primitives.
- 4.5/4.6: normalization and analysis are pure src/core functions. They must be reusable in Node by the pack builder and in the generator worker.
- 4.7: defines the scene-graph group that a component instance maps to.
- 5.1: scene.json v1 includes componentDefs, components, licenseTexts, Part.componentRef (+ materialSlots/comOverrideMm if approved) and Anchor.source 'component'. The bundle gains licenses/.
- 5.2: the Rust zip-guard module is written generically: limits as parameters, allowlist patterns, symlink rejection, counted bytes. 14.2 reuses it.
- 6.2: stable built-in material keys (std.steel, std.abs ...), because packs reference them. Material slots decided here.
- 7.1: anchors get an optional name, interface and role.
- 8.2: the mate tool accepts interface-based suggestions.
- 10.3: the node library is built as a registry of SimModelId@major plus BuiltinSymbolIds.
- 10.5: the expression grammar has the limits above and an AST interpreter.
- 10.6: the part<->node association is stored as a ComponentInstance.
- 11: an unknown model produces a diagnostic, not a crash.
- 12.1: the binding model supports component-local refs and ExternalSlot.

Phase 14, Component library:
- 14.1 zod schemas (component/pack/catalog), validators, limits, fixtures, unit tests. Depends on 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12.
- 14.2 Rust library module: store layout, staging, install-from-file, hash chain, zip guards, GC, cargo tests (zip-slip, symlink, ratio bomb, truncated, unlisted file). Depends on 4.1, 5.2.
- 14.3 Library tab: installed browser, search worker, cards, license popover.
- 14.4 Insertion: pointer-event drag, transient ghost, BVH placement, interface snap suggestions, single undo, designators. E2E with mocked IPC and fixture packs. Depends on 3, 4.6, 8.3.
- 14.5 Save as component, Export/Install pack, harvest from .stvd.
- 14.6 Credits dialog and export credits (GLB asset.copyright/extras, STL sidecar).
- 14.7 Online catalog: explicit refresh, minisign, rollback/expiry, downloads with progress and cancel, updates and revocations. Tested against a local mock server and test keys.
- 14.8 Generators v1 (bearing, fasteners, nut, washer, rod/tube, primitives, spur gear). Depends on 4.5.
- 14.9 Content pipeline repo + CI signing + first catalog. The catalog mirrors node-library v1 (PLAN 10.3): battery, resistor, pot, LED, diode, switch, fuse, DC motor, solenoid/linear actuator, pump, valve, cylinder, emitter/sensor, plus mechanical basics. Depends on 4.4 and all of the above.
- 14.10 Exit criteria: unit, cargo and E2E tests; full build. Stop for user approval.

Optional early slice: 14.1-14.5 limited to geometry + anchors + mates could land right after Phase 8. That would supply realistic content for the Phase 9 200-part benchmark, but it splits the phase. Recommended only if the user wants it.
open_questions: Hosting: a separate repo bmisho/StudioVD-library (recommended: content licenses differ from app code, separate CI, GitHub's 1-5 GB repo guidance, 1000 assets per release) or releases on bmisho/StudioVD itself?

Signing-key custody: offline maintainer signing, or a CI secret in a protected environment? How many keys, and what rotation and compromise policy? (v1 recovery = app update with new keys; no threshold signing.)
Phase order: run Phase 14 between 12 and 13 (recommended), renumber it to 13, or ship an early geometry-only slice after Phase 8?
Multi-material parts (Phase 6): add Part.materialSlots keyed by glTF material name (recommended; also helps STEP/GLB imports with colours), or split per material into fixed-mated parts?
Add Part.comOverrideMm? Datasheet mass plus geometric centroid assumes uniform density, which is wrong for motors and other mixed-material parts.
How is a component instance shown in the scene graph? Phase 4.7 'group' semantics are undefined: is a group a part without an asset, or a separate entity?
Composite (multi-node sub-circuit) block definitions: v1 or schemaVersion 2? Relays and H-bridges are awkward as single expression blocks.

Actuators vs decision D3 (sim never moves parts): servo, motor and linear-actuator components can only show the commanded pose as a ghost or label. Does the user want a future 'sim drives joints' mode? It affects the binding target kinds reserved now.

Official-catalog license allowlist (proposed: CC0, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0 with or without KiCad exception, MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0) needs legal review. Specifically: (a) does ShareAlike reach a user's .stvd or exported GLB containing CC-BY-SA geometry; (b) are renders or screenshots Adapted Material; (c) does the KiCad 'electronic designs' exception cover 3D mechanical assemblies. All UNKNOWN.

Legal status of using ISO/DIN dimension tables inside in-app generators (copyright / EU sui generis database rights): UNKNOWN. Use only permissively licensed table sources (e.g. cq_warehouse, Apache-2.0) with attribution?

Initial catalog scope and budgets: number of components, triangle cap per component (proposed: warn at 50k, reject at 500k per asset), and total download size. All unknown until the pipeline runs. KiCad STEP samples are 24-180 KB.
Default for online access: ask on first use (proposed), on by default, or off by default?
Location of the user library: appLocalDataDir (proposed), Documents, or user-configurable? Should it sync or roam?
User namespace scheme: a random 'u-xxxxxx' per installation (proposed), or a mandatory publisher name? This matters when sharing packs between colleagues.
Extension name .stvdpack (no conflict search done yet), and should single-component share files use a different extension from bundles?
Should packs optionally include original STEP sources (sources/) so users can re-tessellate at another quality? Larger downloads; default no.
Naming policy for vendor names, MPNs and trademarks in the catalog (e.g. generic 'micro servo, 9 g class' vs a brand name).
Angle units in scene.json mates (rad assumed here; PLAN 1.3 just says angleOffset). Confirm in the Phase 8 schema.

'Download only' interpretation: generators and their small dimension tables necessarily ship in the installer as code. Is that acceptable, or should even generator presets be hidden until a catalog is fetched?
Update UX: per-instance and project-wide updates of the same MAJOR in one undo entry, with Replace for MAJOR changes. Should updates also be offered for user-library components across projects?
